predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: Roussillon, 'occupied by the Carolingians in 760' after Pepin the Short's defeat of the Saracens in 759

successors.name: Crown of Aragon
successors.text: the whole county: 'On the death of Gerard II without heirs in 1172, Roussillon passed' to Alfonso II of Aragon

ledger.x: 759: the Carolingian county of Roussillon is established.
817: Gaucelm receives Empúries and the two counties are joined.
989: Gausfred I dies and Empúries is separated from Roussillon.
About 989: Giselbert I moves the seat from Castellrosselló to Perpignan.
1014: Hugh I of Empúries invades Roussillon.
1172: Roussillon passes to Alfonso II of Aragon.
1172: the county of Roussillon ends as a separate state when Alfonso II takes it.

wars.name: Empúries-Roussillon war (1014-1019)
wars.outcome: Hugh I of Empúries invaded Roussillon in 1014; a pact of 1019 made the two counties permanently separate.

certainty.note: A Pyrenean and coastal county whose pages name towns and valleys, not lines; the frontier with Empúries is the best known (separated in 989, pact of 1019) but is still a stand-in outline; the Conflent and Vallespir frontier with Cerdanya…
